claims.text: OpenJDK 21 HashMap source defines hash spreading, power-of-two index calculation, Node table buckets, collision traversal, TreeNode insertion and resize on size exceeding threshold.

OpenJDK 21 HashMap source defines default initial capacity 16, default load factor 0.75, TREEIFY_THRESHOLD 8, UNTREEIFY_THRESHOLD 6, MIN_TREEIFY_CAPACITY 64, and resizes instead of treeifying when the table is smaller than the minimum capacity.

OpenJDK HashMap implementation notes state that tree bins provide worst-case O(log n) operations when keys either have distinct hashes or are orderable; for tied hashes this graceful bound is conditioned on keys being Comparable, so the candidate does not promise O(log n) for many equal-hash non-comparable keys.

OpenJDK 21 HashMap source documents load-factor time/space tradeoffs, TreeNodes as roughly twice the size of regular nodes, that HashMap is not synchronized, and that fail-fast iterators are best-effort bug detection rather than a correctness guarantee.
